issues.title: Build a bootable Yocto image for Raspberry Pi 3 B+ with the edge client
issues.evidence: The user has a Raspberry Pi 3 Model B+ with no confirmed installed image. The current meta-suifleet layer has a client recipe but no Pi image/build configuration; SSH deployment alone does not satisfy the requested boot-from-image test.
acceptance: Provide a version-pinned BitBake build configuration for Raspberry Pi 3 Model B+ using meta-raspberrypi MACHINE=raspberrypi3-64 and a compatible Yocto/toolchain/layer set; validate the board support and locked Rust dependency requirements.

Add a bootable SuiFleet test image recipe that includes the suifleet package built through its cargo BitBake recipe, systemd service, CA certificates, networking and test diagnostics; do not substitute an SSH-copied binary for image integration.

Build and publish the SD-card image with checksum, source/layer revisions, package manifest and flashing/first-boot instructions. Flash only an explicitly selected removable device; no disk writes in ordinary builds.

Provision a unique device key on first boot, never bake private keys into the image, and retain identity/journal across restart. Provide an unenrolled first-boot state that exposes the signer address and waits for valid manifest/device IDs rather than repeatedly starting against placeholders.
Prefer wired Ethernet for the first test, document optional Wi-Fi firmware/configuration, and provide serial or authenticated SSH diagnostics after boot without committing credentials.

Boot the physical Pi from the generated image; verify board/architecture, packaged binary revision/hash, provisioning, service startup after enrollment, networking and persistent state. SSH redeploy is an optional developer loop, not image acceptance.
issues.validation: BitBake parse/build/package/image verification plus a real SD-card first boot on the Raspberry Pi 3 B+. Capture layer revisions, image/package manifests, binary/image hashes, board/OS/architecture and redacted logs. A cross-build or simulator alone does not pass physical-image acceptance.
issues.description: Build a bootable Yocto image for Raspberry Pi 3 B+ with the edge client. Provide a version-pinned BitBake build configuration for Raspberry Pi 3 Model B+ using meta-raspberrypi MACHINE=raspberrypi3-64 and a compatible Yocto/toolchain/layer set; validate the board support and locked Rust dependency requirements.

issues.title: Create a harmless versioned test component for Raspberry Pi OTA
issues.evidence: There is no dedicated test payload that proves which artifact version actually ran on a device.
acceptance: Provide v1/v2 test application artifacts and deterministic recipes with recipe/artifact SHA-256 hashes; report version, run ID and architecture in a structured receipt under the dedicated test directory.
Use the current one-shot apply path without requiring the future supervisor; support injected install failure and health failure without touching boot partitions or unrelated services.
Test the fixture locally and expose a later supervisor/config/rollback mode as those features become available; distinguish successful install from runtime health.

Package required test updater/fixture support through its Yocto recipe for consumption by SF-029. Physical Pi image integration and v1/v2 execution are verified in SF-029/SF-031, which depend on this fixture; they are not completion prerequisites for SF-030.
issues.validation: Local fixture tests verify exact version receipts, deterministic hashes, failure modes and isolated writes; run both versions on the Pi in SF-031.
issues.description: Create a harmless versioned test component for Raspberry Pi OTA. Provide v1/v2 test application artifacts and deterministic recipes with recipe/artifact SHA-256 hashes; report version, run ID and architecture in a structured receipt under the dedicated test directory.

issues.title: Run wallet-to-testnet-to-Raspberry-Pi OTA acceptance tests
issues.evidence: SF-010 specifies live acceptance but there is no concrete Pi test runner joining wallet, Sui, Walrus and a real ARM daemon.
acceptance: Provide an opt-in test runner with local-network and Sui testnet profiles using a verified network manifest, compatible Sui/Walrus endpoints and explicitly supplied funded test accounts; fail preflight clearly when APIs or funding are unavailable.

Boot the physical Raspberry Pi 3 B+ from the SF-029 BitBake-built image containing the SF-025 client package, verify first-boot identity and enroll it, then upload the SF-030 recipe/artifact and exercise direct/group deployments through the actual frontend wallet flow.
Assert execution effects, matching on-chain status and Pi version/run-ID receipts for v1 then v2; record transaction IDs, blob IDs, binary/artifact hashes and redacted device logs.
Exercise offline catch-up, daemon restart, report retry, recipe/artifact tampering, unauthorized targets and failed updater; expected failures must not report Applied.
Keep private keys on their intended host, separate manual wallet steps from unattended test-account automation, document testnet resets/retention, and preserve device identity/journal during cleanup.
Publish a capability-based acceptance matrix so future runtime/config/rollback/self-update features add cases; do not claim this baseline tests every Greengrass feature or A/B firmware safety.

Start the enrolled client before creating the first test deployment so enrollment baseline behavior does not intentionally skip it; verify a fetched/applied test component and matching chain receipt. A read-only authenticated inventory/health query is an optional earlier connectivity smoke test, not OTA acceptance.
issues.validation: Offline harness tests and an actual frontend-wallet -> Sui/Walrus -> Pi -> on-chain receipt run, with reproducible evidence and explicit skipped/blocked cases. Hardware reboot/power-loss tests stay in SF-016.
issues.description:
Run wallet-to-testnet-to-Raspberry-Pi OTA acceptance tests. Provide an opt-in test runner with local-network and Sui testnet profiles using a verified network manifest, compatible Sui/Walrus endpoints and explicitly supplied funded test accounts; fail preflight clearly when APIs or funding are unavailable.

issues.evidence: Implementation workers do not currently dispatch their successors.
acceptance: Automatically dispatch atomic highest-priority eligible claims to bounded configurable Codex/Claude slots.

issues.description:
Workers currently stop after their assigned implementation; the PR coordinator reviews and merges but does not dispatch the next ticket. Add a persistent dispatcher so authorized Codex/Claude implementation slots atomically refresh and claim the highest-priority eligible ticket automatically.

Acceptance:
- Configurable project/family/model worker slots; atomic claims remain authoritative; no duplicate workers or recovery of expired/blocked claims.
- Durable process/claim receipts survive restarts and detect failed launches; heartbeat live ownership, stop dispatch for failed/orphaned workers rather than silently reclaiming.
- Completed implementation hands off to existing independent review/feedback/merge service; next implementation may begin once the previous process stops and ownership reaches Review/Done.
- Existing manual workers and claims count against configured implementation concurrency; pending review repairs have priority; no new issues, deployment or hardware programming inferred.
- Explicit enable/disable, status, bounded polling/backoff and idle handling; account/SSH isolation per project; secrets never persisted in receipts/logs.
- Meaningful offline tests for concurrency, failures, restart, no eligible work and safe progression. Document and install the service here under user authorization.
